Title: Extended-Duration Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Acutely Ill Medical Patients With Recently Reduced Mobility: A Randomized Trial (EXCLAIM)
Author: Hull et al.
Comment: The paper reports only an absolute risk difference, not a risk ratio or odds ratio, for major bleeding; no RR/OR was recorded since none was reported. Denominators are the safety population (patients randomized who received ≥1 dose: 2975 vs 2988), which the paper treats as the primary safety analysis population; the full randomized total was 6085. Counts correspond to the post hoc 20-g/L hemoglobin-decrease definition used in the paper's main tables.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Extended-duration enoxaparin 40 mg/d subcutaneously for 28 ± 4 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: inpatient hospital with some outpatient continuation of prophylaxis
Country: Multinational (370 sites in 20 countries: North/South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Middle East, Australia)
Participant type: Acutely ill medical patients aged ≥40 years with recently reduced mobility (level 1 or level 2 immobility)
Recruitment source: 370 hospitals across 20 countries, February 2002 to March 2006
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with a major bleeding event / total in arm (safety population), Total Population row
effect_direction: Higher major bleeding with extended-duration enoxaparin (25/2975, 0.8%) than placebo (10/2988, 0.3%) — harmful for the treatment arm

Report_ID: Major bleeding (ISTH criteria) within 35 days — primary safety outcome
Title: Rivaroxaban versus no anticoagulation for post-discharge thromboprophylaxis after hospitalisation for COVID-19 (MICHELLE): an open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled trial
Author: Ramacciotti E, et al. (MICHELLE investigators)
Comment: Zero major bleeding events in BOTH arms; the paper itself reports the relative risk as 'NA' (not applicable) in Table 2, so this is not estimable as a ratio measure and per the synthesis plan should be excluded from RR pooling rather than continuity-corrected. Denominators are the ITT population (159 per arm) rather than the 160 per arm randomised.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rivaroxaban 10 mg/day for 35 days after discharge (extended-duration thromboprophylaxis)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); zero events in both arms -- not estimable for a ratio measure (Cochrane convention: excluded from pooling, not continuity-corrected)
Design Type: open-label randomised controlled trial (1:1), blinded adjudication
Study Environment: multicentre clinical (hospital discharge and outpatient follow-up)
Participant type: Adults hospitalised ≥3 days for COVID-19 at increased VTE risk (modified IMPROVE VTE score ≥4, or 2–3 with D-dimer >500 ng/mL), all having received standard in-hospital parenteral heparin prophylaxis
Recruitment source: 14 hospitals in Brazil, at hospital discharge
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with an adjudicated ISTH major bleeding event / total analysed per arm
Outcome variable: Major bleeding (ISTH criteria) within 35 days — primary safety outcome
effect_direction: No events in either arm (0/159 vs 0/159) — no difference observed

Report_ID: Major bleeding during the 30-day treatment period (short-term, ≤45 days)
Title: Apixaban versus Enoxaparin for Thromboprophylaxis in Medically Ill Patients
Author: Goldhaber SZ, Leizorovicz A, Kakkar AK, Haas SK, Merli G, Knabb RM, Weitz JI
Comment: Denominators are the treated (safety) population (3184 apixaban / 3217 enoxaparin), not the randomized population (3255 / 3273), as the paper's safety analysis was prespecified on patients receiving ≥1 dose. Treatment period = 30 days, within the ≤45-day short-term window.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily for 30 days (extended-duration prophylaxis)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trial
Participant type: Acutely ill hospitalized medical patients ≥40 years with congestive heart failure, respiratory failure, infection, acute rheumatic disorder, or inflammatory bowel disease and restricted mobility
Recruitment source: 302 hospital centers in 35 countries, June 2007 – February 2011
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with an adjudicated major bleeding event / total treated patients per arm
Outcome variable: Major bleeding during the 30-day treatment period (short-term, ≤45 days)
effect_direction: Higher major bleeding with extended apixaban (15/3184, 0.47%) than standard enoxaparin (6/3217, 0.19%); RR 2.58 (1.02–7.24) — harmful for treatment arm

Title: Rivaroxaban for Thromboprophylaxis in Acutely Ill Medical Patients (MAGELLAN)
Author: Cohen AT, et al. (MAGELLAN Investigators)
Comment: P value reported as "<0.001"; recorded as 0.001 (upper bound). Denominators are the safety population (received ≥1 dose: 3997 and 4001), slightly smaller than the randomized population (4050 and 4051). Relative risk is Mantel–Haenszel weighted with stratification by geographic region.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Extended-duration oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for 35±4 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Hospitalized patients ≥40 years of age with acute medical illness and reduced mobility
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients with any major bleeding event up to day 35 (within 2 days after last dose)
effect_direction: Higher major bleeding with extended rivaroxaban (43/3997, 1.1%) than standard enoxaparin-placebo (15/4001, 0.4%); RR 2.9 (1.60–5.15) — harmful for treatment arm

Title: Extended Thromboprophylaxis with Betrixaban in Acutely Ill Medical Patients (APEX)
Author: Cohen AT, Harrington RA, Goldhaber SZ, Hull RD, Wiens BL, Gold A, Hernandez AF, Gibson CM
Comment: Denominators are the safety population (3716 per arm, patients receiving ≥1 dose of active drug), not the randomized Ns (3759/3754), because the paper reports major bleeding only in the safety population. Bleeding window is "up to 7 days after the last dose of a study drug" (i.e., ~day 42-49), which approximates but may slightly exceed the plan's ≤45-day short-term window.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Extended-duration betrixaban 80 mg once daily for 35-42 days (plus enoxaparin placebo)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults ≥40 years hospitalized <96 hours for acute medical illness with reduced mobility and VTE risk factors
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with an adjudicated major bleeding event / total in safety population per arm
effect_direction: Slightly higher major bleeding with extended betrixaban (25/3716, 0.7%) vs standard enoxaparin (21/3716, 0.6%); RR 1.19 (0.67–2.12), not significant

Report_ID: Principal safety outcome: major bleeding (through day 45)
Title: Rivaroxaban for Thromboprophylaxis after Hospitalization for Medical Illness (MARINER)
Author: Spyropoulos et al. (MARINER Investigators)
Comment: Paper reports a Cox hazard ratio, not a risk ratio; no RR is named in the paper, so risk_ratio was left empty and raw event counts were recorded for downstream RR pooling. Denominators are the safety population (5982/5980), which differ slightly from the ITT randomized totals (6007/6012).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily (7.5 mg if CrCl 30 to <50 ml/min) for 45 days after discharge (extended duration)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Medically ill patients >=40 years hospitalized 3-10 days (heart failure, respiratory insufficiency/COPD exacerbation, ischemic stroke, infectious or inflammatory disease) at increased VTE risk (modified IMPROVE score >=4, or 2-3 plus elevated d-dimer), who received in-hospital LMWH/UFH prophylaxis
Recruitment source: 671 hospital centers in 36 countries, June 2014 - January 2018
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with an adjudicated major bleeding event / total patients in arm during the 45-day treatment phase
Outcome variable: Principal safety outcome: major bleeding (through day 45)
additional_group_ns: ITT efficacy denominators were 6007 (rivaroxaban) and 6012 (placebo); the major bleeding analysis used the safety population (5982 and 5980).
effect_direction: Higher major bleeding with extended rivaroxaban (17/5982, 0.28%) than placebo (9/5980, 0.15%); HR 1.88 (0.84–4.23) — harmful direction for treatment arm, not significant

Title: Two models of thromboprophylaxis in acutely ill medical inpatients
Author: Luba, Firek, Kochanowski
Comment: Zero major bleeding events in BOTH arms (0/150 vs 0/150) — not estimable as a risk ratio; should be excluded from RR pooling rather than continuity-corrected. Per-arm counts are not given in a table; they are derived from the paper's explicit narrative statement that there were no major bleedings in either group, combined with the stated per-group randomized N of 150 each. No test statistic or p-value reported for this outcome.; zero events in both arms -- not estimable for a ratio measure (Cochrane convention: excluded from pooling, not continuity-corrected)
Participant type: Acutely ill medical inpatients aged >40 years with expected immobilization of at least 3 days (cancer patients excluded)
Recruitment source: Consecutive medical inpatients, Municipal Hospital, Rabka-Zdrój, Poland
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with a major bleeding event / total randomized per arm
effect_direction: No major bleeding events in either arm (0/150 extended vs 0/150 standard) — no difference observed
